scope_note: Daily edition from matching Tuesday /new listings: 316 non-replacement cs.CV rows, 88 cs.RO rows, 386 deduplicated papers, and 311 ROI papers. Tier A cards are conservative abstract-only autopsies from the repository parser output; no figure, table, full-text, code, or dataset-release claims are asserted.
executive_thesis: The September 1 batch turns perception and robot learning into release-contract design. Geometry papers ask whether a representation can preserve metric state, topology, temporal order, and optical failure information well enough for a robot to act. VLA and driving papers expose a different failure: high-scoring demonstrations, traffic-rule averages, or stream samples can push a policy update away from safe behavior unless the update is made eligible by the right evidence. Tactile and dexterous world-model papers make contact sensing and visuo-tactile data infrastructure first-class assets. VLM papers move from global visual tokens to state-conditioned evidence retrieval, while robustness papers separate nuisance shift, compression loss, calibration attack, and dense-prediction structure before deployment claims are trusted. APRL's opening is to own the evaluation harness where geometry, contact, memory, and evidence gates decide when an autonomous system may continue.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Geometry must survive action use
decision_cards.body: SkyReg, ReconSplat, RoSe-SLAM, OptiGeo, SeqAlign3DVG, and VISTA all reject the idea that a visually plausible 3D product is enough; each makes coordinate alignment, dynamic mapping, ordered grounding, optical degradation, or missing depth an action-facing variable.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Policy updates need eligibility evidence
decision_cards.body: Multi-trajectory VLA driving, RedLight-VLA, FrameScope, AdaptAV, InfraOcc, and Driving on Memory all ask which rare event, stream frame, oracle label, static scaffold, or memory variable should be allowed to change a policy before the next deployment decision.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Embodiment needs contact assets
decision_cards.body: Haptic Foundation Models, N0-Foundation, Motus2, AnyWorld, sliding palpation, and tactile sensors move robot learning away from vision-only imitation and toward reusable contact data, tactile representations, and world-model interfaces that can be inspected after failure.

papers.title: Pixel-wise Geo-registration of Drone and Satellite Images
papers.fit: dense geo-registration - drone/satellite alignment - metric map supervision
papers.status_quo: Cross-view localization is often judged by one GPS coordinate for a whole image.
papers.friction: The abstract says that single-coordinate labels leave dense geodetic alignment underexplored even when every pixel may need a real-world location.
papers.hidden_premise: A robot or UAV map is actionable only if image evidence remains aligned at the pixel and coordinate-frame level.
papers.conceptual_move: Move cross-view localization from image-level retrieval to pixel-wise geo-registration with dense supervision.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes SkyReg as a dataset and benchmark with per-pixel geo-location supervision across orthographic, perspective, urban, rural, and mixed settings.

evidence.claim: Existing benchmarks largely provide only GPS labels, limiting evaluation to one coordinate per image.
SkyReg provides dense per-pixel geo-location supervision for drone-to-satellite registration.
APRL should evaluate aerial mapping by downstream route and relocalization error, not image retrieval alone.

papers.falsification: If dense pixel alignment does not improve route reuse or relocalization under viewpoint changes, the benchmark may be over-serving map aesthetics.
papers.adversarial: Stress repetitive roads, altitude changes, partial occlusion, and weather differences where image-level retrieval can appear correct while local alignment fails.
papers.thinking_tool: Ask whether each pixel can be put into the coordinate system used by navigation.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for UAV and outdoor mapping; less direct for indoor manipulation without a global geodetic frame.

papers.title: RoSe-SLAM: Robust Semantic-Aware Gaussian Splatting SLAM from Dynamic Monocular Videos
papers.fit: Gaussian SLAM - dynamic scenes - semantic tracking and mapping
papers.status_quo: Many SLAM and Gaussian mapping systems assume static scene structure when fusing observations.
papers.friction: The abstract says conventional SLAM accuracy degrades in dynamic and unstructured environments because static assumptions fail.
papers.hidden_premise: Semantic features from foundation models can identify which visual evidence should influence tracking and mapping in dynamic scenes.
papers.conceptual_move: Turn Gaussian Splatting SLAM into a semantic-aware dynamic-scene filtering and reconstruction problem.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes distilling semantic features from a 2D foundation model to enhance dynamic tracking and mapping performance.

evidence.claim: The paper identifies dynamic and unstructured scenes as a source of SLAM degeneration.
RoSe-SLAM uses semantic scene understanding from uncalibrated monocular inputs.
APRL should treat map updates as decisions that can reject transient or dynamic evidence.

papers.falsification: If semantic filtering preserves visual quality but not camera tracking or relocalization under dynamic objects, the action-facing claim is weak.
papers.adversarial: Use moving people, repeated texture, and temporary occluders to test whether semantic updates prevent map corruption rather than only clean renderings.
papers.thinking_tool: A map update is a controlled action, not passive accumulation.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for mobile robots and dynamic mapping; weaker for static object scans where transient evidence is absent.

papers.title: Aligning Multi-Trajectory Supervision with Policy Optimization for VLA Driving
papers.fit: VLA driving - multi-trajectory supervision - GRPO alignment
papers.status_quo: Multi-trajectory imitation treats high-scoring candidate futures as broadly useful supervision for a driving policy.
papers.friction: The abstract says some high-scoring trajectories can degrade later GRPO because their advantage estimates are misaligned with what the current policy can safely realize.
papers.hidden_premise: A demonstration should become policy supervision only when it is feasible under the current policy distribution and safe-behavior constraints.
papers.conceptual_move: Move VLA driving supervision from best-looking trajectory selection to policy-optimization-aligned eligibility.
papers.mechanism: The abstract frames the method as correcting policy-gradient bias induced by infeasible noisy trajectories.

evidence.claim: High-scoring trajectories can induce advantage estimates misaligned with the current policy's feasible behavior distribution.
The paper proposes aligning multi-trajectory supervision with policy optimization.
APRL should test whether selected demonstrations change safe recovery behavior, not only imitation loss.

papers.falsification: If alignment improves only benchmark reward but not rare unsafe maneuver recovery, it may still be optimizing the wrong eligibility signal.
papers.adversarial: Construct visually plausible but infeasible trajectory candidates at intersections and measure policy drift from safe compliant behavior.
papers.thinking_tool: A good demonstration is not automatically a good policy update.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLA driving and robot policies trained with multiple candidate futures; less direct for deterministic expert demonstrations.

papers.title: RedLight-VLA: Models for traffic-rule grounding and behavioral emphasis in driving policies
papers.fit: traffic-rule grounding - rare maneuver weighting - VLA driving
papers.status_quo: Behavior cloning averages trajectory loss over common driving behavior, so rare rule-governed events can be underweighted.
papers.friction: The abstract says braking and launching at signalized intersections contribute little to averaged trajectory loss and fused representations lack explicit traffic-light and stop-line supervision.
papers.hidden_premise: Rare legal maneuvers need explicit behavioral emphasis and perception targets even when manual rule annotation is unavailable.
papers.conceptual_move: Reframe driving VLA training around rare traffic-rule state and longitudinal behavior rather than average trajectory fit.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes trajectory-derived behavioral reweighting and generated perception targets for governing traffic-light and stop-line state.

evidence.claim: Behavior-cloned VLA driving policies struggle with rare rule-governed maneuvers at signalized intersections.
The method emphasizes rare deceleration and acceleration using trajectory-derived behavioral reweighting.
APRL should evaluate whether rule evidence changes the policy before a red-light violation, not after a final score.

papers.falsification: If the reweighting helps only canonical intersections and fails on occluded or unusual signal layouts, it may memorize scenario templates.
papers.adversarial: Vary stop-line visibility, traffic-light phase ambiguity, lead-vehicle motion, and launch timing while measuring violation-before-action signals.
papers.thinking_tool: Make rare rule states loud enough to compete with average imitation loss.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for driving policies; transferable to manipulation only when rare safety states can be derived from trajectory structure.

papers.title: $\mathcal{N}_0$-Foundation: Towards the Age of Tactile Intelligence
papers.fit: tactile foundation model - data infrastructure - embodied manipulation
papers.status_quo: Generalist robot learning often treats touch as an auxiliary sensor behind vision and language.
papers.friction: The abstract says tactile-enabled embodied manipulation needs sensing hardware, large-scale multimodal data, tactile representation learning, and standardized evaluation together.
papers.hidden_premise: Touch becomes a foundation-model substrate only when hardware, data collection, representation learning, and benchmarks are co-designed.
papers.conceptual_move: Move tactile manipulation from task-specific sensing to an integrated tactile intelligence infrastructure.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes a vision-based tactile sensor, tactile UMI, synchronized visuo-tactile collection, NeoData, and standardized evaluation.

evidence.claim: The paper integrates tactile sensing hardware, large-scale multimodal data, tactile representation learning, and standardized evaluation.
It reports NeoData with synchronized visual and tactile data across robot embodiments and UMI demonstrations.
APRL should treat tactile data as a reusable asset with contact-failure labels, not an add-on sensor stream.

papers.falsification: If tactile representations do not separate visually identical contact states, the infrastructure may not justify its collection cost.
papers.adversarial: Use transparent, deformable, slippery, and small industrial components where visual features are ambiguous but contact traces should differ.
papers.thinking_tool: Ask what touch can disambiguate that vision cannot observe.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for contact-rich manipulation and inspection; weaker for navigation tasks with sparse physical contact.

papers.title: Motus2: A Self-Evolving General World Model for Dexterous Manipulation
papers.fit: dexterous manipulation - self-evolving world model - policy/simulator/evaluator loop
papers.status_quo: World models are often used as simulators with an action head appended afterward.
papers.friction: The abstract says existing models typically append action output to a world simulator without coupling perception, prediction, action, evaluation, and improvement into a closed decision-and-learning loop.
papers.hidden_premise: A manipulation world model is more useful when policy, simulator, and evaluator share a loop that can improve from its own interaction evidence.
papers.conceptual_move: Turn the world model from a rollout generator into a self-evolving manipulation system with multiple control interfaces.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes shared-weight interfaces for policy, action-conditioned simulation, and evaluation, plus model and data scaling.

evidence.claim: General embodied agents should perceive, predict, act, evaluate, and improve within a unified system.
Motus2 exposes policy, simulator, and evaluation interfaces in one self-evolving world model.
APRL should score whether evaluator feedback changes later dexterous behavior, not only video prediction quality.

papers.falsification: If self-evolution improves simulated rollouts but not contact-rich real or held-out manipulation, the evaluator may reinforce simulator shortcuts.
papers.adversarial: Use object slip, hidden contact, and tactile-only disambiguation where visual rollouts can look correct while manipulation fails.
papers.thinking_tool: World models should leave an inspectable improvement trace after each failed action.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for dexterous manipulation; less direct for perception-only systems without action feedback.

papers.title: CGFM-Nav: Cognitive Graph-Field Memory for Semantic-Guided Lifelong Multimodal Embodied Navigation
papers.fit: lifelong navigation - graph-field memory - semantic retrieval and exploration
papers.status_quo: Navigation systems often separate explicit semantic memory from continuous spatial exploration guidance.
papers.friction: The abstract says current environment representations struggle to jointly support accumulated observations, target retrieval, and continuous exploration in unseen regions.
papers.hidden_premise: Long-horizon navigation needs a memory substrate that is both relational and spatially continuous.
papers.conceptual_move: Represent navigation memory as a coupled multimodal scene graph and continuous graph field.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes organizing objects, spatial relations, and visual observations into a persistent scene representation for target retrieval and long-horizon reasoning.

evidence.claim: VLN requires agents to reason over accumulated observations while exploring unseen regions.
CGFM couples explicit relational memory with continuous spatial intuition.
APRL should test whether memory improves recovery after revisiting changed or ambiguous spaces.

papers.falsification: If graph-field memory improves only target lookup but not route recovery under changed layouts, it is not enough for lifelong deployment.
papers.adversarial: Evaluate repeated visits, moved objects, misleading semantic priors, and dead-end exploration where old memory can become harmful.
papers.thinking_tool: Navigation memory should be scored by recovery value, not storage completeness.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for VLN/ObjectNav and field robots; weaker for one-shot paths with no revisits.

papers.title: State-Conditioned Visual Evidence Retrieval for Fine-Grained Perception in Document Vision-Language Models
papers.fit: VLM evidence retrieval - decoding-state conditioning - document perception
papers.status_quo: Document VLMs repeatedly access globally compressed visual tokens while decoding fine-grained answers.
papers.friction: The abstract says visual evidence for each prediction is localized and conditioned on the current decoding state, but current representations are accessed in full every step.
papers.hidden_premise: A perception system should retrieve only the evidence that can change the current prediction state.
papers.conceptual_move: Formulate fine-grained perception as state-conditioned retrieval instead of global visual-token reuse.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes retrieving visual evidence conditioned on the current decoding state for document parsing.

evidence.claim: Document parsing demands fine-grained visual perception beyond typical vision-language tasks.
Visual evidence for each prediction is localized and conditioned on current decoding state.
APRL can reuse this idea for robot perception queries where only some cues are action-changing.

papers.falsification: If state-conditioned retrieval saves compute but misses rare safety cues, the evidence policy is efficient but unsafe.
papers.adversarial: Test cluttered labels, visually similar objects, and action preconditions where a small missed region flips the decision.
papers.thinking_tool: Evidence value is conditional on the decision currently being made.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for fine-grained VLM parsing and robot grounding; less direct for dense regression without discrete prediction states.

papers.title: Think, Look, and Revise: Inconsistency-Aware Visual Self-Correction in MLLMs
papers.fit: MLLM self-correction - tool verification - inconsistency detection
papers.status_quo: Tool-augmented multimodal reasoning often trusts external tool outputs as if they were reliable evidence.
papers.friction: The abstract says existing approaches rarely verify tool outputs, limiting their ability to detect and recover from perceptual tool failures.
papers.hidden_premise: A visual reasoning system needs a separate inconsistency signal before it can safely revise a tool-supported answer.
papers.conceptual_move: Turn visual self-correction into a loop that detects inconsistency between model reasoning, visual evidence, and tool outputs.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes ReVISE as an inconsistency-aware framework for multimodal reasoning with external tools.

evidence.claim: Existing tool-augmented approaches rarely verify tool outputs.
The paper proposes inconsistency-aware visual self-correction.
APRL should require robot VLM agents to localize which evidence or tool output triggered revision.

papers.falsification: If revisions mainly follow model confidence rather than visual inconsistency, the system may still be self-reporting uncertainty.
papers.adversarial: Inject depth, detector, and OCR tool errors that are plausible but action-critical, then measure whether the agent revises before acting.
papers.thinking_tool: Do not repair a decision until the inconsistent evidence has a name.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for tool-using VLM agents; weaker for closed-form perception modules without external tool calls.

papers.title: NFAD: Nuisance-Filtered Anomaly Detection Under Distribution Shift
papers.fit: anomaly detection - nuisance shift - deployment reliability
papers.status_quo: Industrial anomaly detection benchmarks often assume controlled acquisition conditions and near-saturated benchmark performance.
papers.friction: The abstract says illumination, background, viewpoint, and other environmental shifts can move normal samples away from the learned normal distribution and cause false anomaly responses.
papers.hidden_premise: A deployment-ready anomaly detector must separate defect evidence from nuisance variation before raising an alarm.
papers.conceptual_move: Reframe anomaly detection under distribution shift as nuisance filtering in feature space.
papers.mechanism: The abstract describes explicitly modeling nuisance variation from changing imaging conditions without source data or target labels.

evidence.claim: Strong benchmark performance does not necessarily transfer to real-world deployment.
Environmental factors can shift normal samples and cause false anomaly responses.
APRL should separate environmental nuisance from physical failure before using anomaly alarms as robot release gates.

papers.falsification: If nuisance filtering suppresses real defects under coupled lighting and geometry changes, the alarm becomes safer-looking but less useful.
papers.adversarial: Pair true small defects with illumination, viewpoint, and background shifts to test false suppression and false alarm trade-offs.
papers.thinking_tool: An alarm should say what changed: the world, the sensor, or the object.
papers.transfer_boundary: Direct for inspection and safety gates; less direct for policy learning unless alarms control action permission.

synthesis.title: Metric and semantic geometry are converging
synthesis.facts: The abstracts expose dense geo-registration, unobserved-view reconstruction, dynamic semantic Gaussian SLAM, optical depth failures, and temporally aligned 3D grounding.
synthesis.inference: The shared decision is to score geometry by whether a later robot state, route, grounding decision, or map update remains valid.

synthesis.title: Robot updates now require evidence eligibility
synthesis.links: VLA driving - RedLight-VLA - FrameScope - AdaptAV - Driving on Memory
synthesis.facts: The papers identify infeasible trajectories, rare traffic-rule events, temporally valuable stream frames, cloud oracle retraining, and memory variables as update selectors.
synthesis.inference: APRL should benchmark not only whether adaptation helps, but which evidence is allowed to change the deployed policy.

synthesis.title: Contact, memory, and alarms are becoming durable lab assets
synthesis.links: N0-Foundation - Motus2 - CGFM-Nav - state-conditioned retrieval - NFAD
synthesis.facts: The batch includes tactile data infrastructure, self-evolving dexterous world models, persistent navigation memory, conditional evidence retrieval, and nuisance-filtered anomaly detection.
synthesis.inference: The lab asset should be a reusable release-gate suite where contact traces, memory state, visual evidence, and nuisance labels explain failures before final success changes.

frontier_memory.label: Strengthening
frontier_memory.history: August 24-31 repeatedly emphasized robot-usable geometry, execution diagnosis, world-model memory, and external safety gates.
frontier_memory.body: September 1 strengthens that axis with dense geo-registration, dynamic Gaussian SLAM, optic-failure depth, tactile infrastructure, and state-conditioned VLM evidence retrieval.

frontier_memory.label: New signal
frontier_memory.history: Recent editions discussed VLA and world-model memory mostly through visual or language evidence.
frontier_memory.body: Today adds a stronger tactile/contact layer: N0-Foundation, Haptic Foundation Models, sliding palpation, and compact tactile sensors frame touch as infrastructure rather than an accessory.

frontier_memory.label: Commoditizing
frontier_memory.history: Compression, cache acceleration, and efficient perception have appeared throughout the last four weeks.
frontier_memory.body: The differentiator is no longer smaller representations alone; it is whether compressed features preserve occupancy, event timing, semantic targets, and action-changing evidence.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: The repo still tends to discuss geometry, VLA adaptation, tactile sensing, and anomaly gates as separate opportunities.
frontier_memory.body: APRL can own their intersection: a release protocol where map state, tactile contact, memory, and evidence retrieval jointly decide whether to act or adapt.

strategy.title: Metric-state geometry release suite
strategy.thesis: Make drone, SLAM, optical-depth, and 3D grounding systems prove that their geometry remains usable for route, grasp, and relocalization decisions.
strategy.one_week: Build a small set of drone-satellite, dynamic indoor, transparent-object, and ordered 3D grounding probes with known metric perturbations.
strategy.one_week_probe: Build a small set of drone-satellite, dynamic indoor, transparent-object, and ordered 3D grounding probes with known metric perturbations.
strategy.four_week: Compare geo-registration, Gaussian SLAM, feed-forward reconstruction, monocular depth, and 3D grounding on downstream route reuse, grasp error, and relocalization.
strategy.four_week_build: Compare geo-registration, Gaussian SLAM, feed-forward reconstruction, monocular depth, and 3D grounding on downstream route reuse, grasp error, and relocalization.
strategy.success: At least one method ranking reverses when judged by downstream robot state error instead of reconstruction or answer score.
strategy.success_metric: At least one method ranking reverses when judged by downstream robot state error instead of reconstruction or answer score.
strategy.stop: If all downstream decisions track ordinary reconstruction metrics under every perturbation, narrow the suite to dynamic-scene SLAM only.
strategy.stop_condition: If all downstream decisions track ordinary reconstruction metrics under every perturbation, narrow the suite to dynamic-scene SLAM only.
strategy.paper_path: A robot-state release-gate paper connecting metric geometry, dynamic maps, and ordered grounding to action validity.
strategy.asset_path: Dense geo labels, dynamic-map clips, transparent-object depth cases, ordered 3D grounding sequences, perturbation scripts, and robot-state outcomes.
strategy.asset: Dense geo labels, dynamic-map clips, transparent-object depth cases, ordered 3D grounding sequences, perturbation scripts, and robot-state outcomes.

strategy.title: Contact-state foundation asset
strategy.thesis: Treat tactile foundation models and dexterous world models as a shared contact-state dataset and evaluator rather than a collection of sensors.
strategy.one_week: Capture a small visuo-tactile manipulation set with transparent, deformable, slippery, and sub-centimetre components under paired visual aliases.
strategy.one_week_probe: Capture a small visuo-tactile manipulation set with transparent, deformable, slippery, and sub-centimetre components under paired visual aliases.
strategy.four_week: Evaluate tactile representations, dexterous world-model feedback, real-to-sim demonstration generation, and tactile anomaly detectors on the same contact-failure labels.
strategy.four_week_build: Evaluate tactile representations, dexterous world-model feedback, real-to-sim demonstration generation, and tactile anomaly detectors on the same contact-failure labels.
strategy.success: Tactile/contact state predicts or separates at least two failures that a vision-only policy treats as identical.
strategy.success_metric: Tactile/contact state predicts or separates at least two failures that a vision-only policy treats as identical.
strategy.stop: If contact traces add no predictive value beyond visual geometry and force thresholds, keep tactile sensing for narrow inspection tasks only.
strategy.stop_condition: If contact traces add no predictive value beyond visual geometry and force thresholds, keep tactile sensing for narrow inspection tasks only.
strategy.paper_path: A tactile-world-model paper centered on contact-state disambiguation and evaluator feedback.
strategy.asset_path: Synchronized video, tactile imprints, contact labels, visual aliases, digital-twin variants, and failure-to-recovery traces.
strategy.asset: Synchronized video, tactile imprints, contact labels, visual aliases, digital-twin variants, and failure-to-recovery traces.

strategy.title: Evidence-eligible autonomy update gate
strategy.thesis: Before a driving or robot policy adapts, identify which rare rule state, stream frame, oracle label, memory variable, or nuisance-filtered alarm makes the update safe.
strategy.one_week: Create paired driving and manipulation episodes where candidate updates are supported by different evidence sources but lead to conflicting action changes.
strategy.one_week_probe: Create paired driving and manipulation episodes where candidate updates are supported by different evidence sources but lead to conflicting action changes.
strategy.four_week: Compare trajectory eligibility, rare-rule reweighting, stream active learning, cloud-oracle adaptation, state-conditioned retrieval, and nuisance-filtered alarms in one update protocol.
strategy.four_week_build: Compare trajectory eligibility, rare-rule reweighting, stream active learning, cloud-oracle adaptation, state-conditioned retrieval, and nuisance-filtered alarms in one update protocol.
strategy.success: The protocol rejects at least one high-scoring but unsafe update and accepts one rare-event update that improves recovery.
strategy.success_metric: The protocol rejects at least one high-scoring but unsafe update and accepts one rare-event update that improves recovery.
strategy.stop: If update eligibility collapses to final reward or confidence, split adaptation from safety gating and publish the negative result.
strategy.stop_condition: If update eligibility collapses to final reward or confidence, split adaptation from safety gating and publish the negative result.
strategy.paper_path: A release-gated autonomy adaptation paper connecting VLA driving, stream learning, and conditional evidence retrieval.
strategy.asset_path: Candidate trajectories, rare-rule labels, stream valuation metadata, oracle disagreements, memory states, nuisance labels, and before-action decisions.
strategy.asset: Candidate trajectories, rare-rule labels, stream valuation metadata, oracle disagreements, memory states, nuisance labels, and before-action decisions.
